verdict.rationale: Typesense Cloud's pricing model is explicitly dedicated-cluster based with 'no limits on records or operations' (docs-20), and since Typesense is also open-source and self-hostable (docs-25, gh-2), founders can run it on their own infra with cost tied to compute/storage rather than per-query billing — directly addressing the fear of per-request cliffs. However there's no independent or community evidence validating actual cost predictability at scale (e.g., a founder confirming bills stayed flat as traffic grew), and the docs don't detail how cluster-tier upgrades are priced as data grows. Missing for 10: independent cost-at-scale testimonials, detailed tier-upgrade pricing mechanics, comparison of self-hosted infra cost trajectory vs query volume.
